newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IG Metall branch agrees job measures.
newsitem.headline: German IG Metall branch agrees job measures.

text.p: The German metal and engineering trade union IG Metall said on Wednesday one of its regional wage committees had agreed measures with employers aimed at protecting employment levels in the sector.

Job protection was named earlier this month by IG Metall as the main focus of its 1997 wage demand and was one of the sticking points in failed national talks between it and the Gesamtmetall employers group.

IG Metall in the state of Lower Saxony said they had agreed with employer representatives in the region a measure that would allow employers in some cases to reduce factory working hours if business conditions were poor.

In contrast to previous agreements of this type, wages of those workers affected will also be cut accordingly. The measure is designed to avoid the need for mass worker lay-offs in business down-turns.
Employers for their part committed themselves to increasing the number of trainee posts by an unspecified amount.

Talks between unions and employers in the industry are proceeding at the regional level following the collapse of central talks earlier this month aimed at getting agreement on proposed sick pay cuts and the wider 1997 wage deal.
IG Metall officials in the southern state of Baden-Wuerttemberg said earlier this week there was a "strong chance" of a deal on job protection measures in that region too.
